verdict.rationale: Qodo documents its own event-driven automation, but only within code review. It automatically reviews every pull request, lets users control when reviews run (manually or automatically), can auto-publish risk labels, and is configurable via the portal or a .pr_agent.toml file. There is no evidence of general, user-defined rules that map arbitrary events to arbitrary actions; its 'rule system' covers coding standards, not event triggers. Missing for 10: user-definable event→action rules beyond PR review triggers, a documented catalog of trigger events and actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Trigger a Qodo code review manually or automatically, and control when reviews run on a pull request.
Once connected, Qodo automatically reviews every pull request
Qodo automatically classifies the risk of a code change and can publish it as a native label in the pull request
Manage Qodo configuration as code using a .pr\_agent.toml file at the repository, project, group, or organization level.
